subject: Scoped access decomposition and RBAC custodian mapping requested for Quantum Health SIG
messages:
From: Alex Bryce <alex.bryce@quantumhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@quantumhealth.com
Date: 2026-12-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: SIG request: RBAC custodian mapping + SCIM delta artifacts

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for taking our SIG intake. To complete our assessment we need a few scoped artifacts from the Redwood side focused on access control and provisioning. Can you please provide the following by EOD Monday, Dec 8? If that timeline is tight let me know and we can extend.

Required:
- SCIM delta export (CSV) showing user provisioning/deprovisioning + attribute changes for the last 30 days. We need deltas with timestamps and actor ids.
- Representative SAML assertion snippets for both normal user logins and machine/service-account flows (include NameID, attributes, issuer, and audience).
- RBAC role-to-owner mapping (who is the role owner/approver) with last attestation date.
- Short narrative (1-2 paragraphs) describing how least-privilege is enforced for role elevation and how service accounts are scoped.

Optional but helpful: examples of automation or policy enforcement (screenshots or links to runbooks).

Attachments: example SIG template (we'll accept small samples).

Appreciate it — we want to close this piece before our internal review on Dec 15.

Best,
Alex
Alex Bryce
Security Manager | Quantum Health
alex.bryce@quantumhealth.com

---
[Attachment: sig_request_template.pdf (PDF)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Bryce <alex.bryce@quantumhealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG request: RBAC custodian mapping + SCIM delta artifacts

Alex — thanks for the clear list. We're on it and can deliver the scoped artifacts you requested. Quick plan:

1) Naomi will pull a 30-day SCIM delta CSV and a sanitized sample (we'll redact PII and keep internal actor ids).
2) We'll export a short set of SAML assertion snippets for both interactive and service-account flows and include commentary on fields.
3) Marissa will extract the RBAC owner matrix and last-attestation timestamps.
4) I'll draft the least-privilege narrative and include links to our runbook and the attestation workflow (Jira ticket links).

Can you confirm whether the SCIM delta can be sanitized (hashing user emails) or you need unhashed values? We typically provide hashed identities for external reviews unless a signed NDA is in place.

Deliverables (ETA): initial package by 2026-12-08 EOD (sanitized). If you need unhashed, we will need a short legal review (+2 business days).

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

---
[Attachment: redwood_sig_checklist.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Bryce <alex.bryce@quantumhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T08:26:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG request: RBAC custodian mapping + SCIM delta artifacts

Hi Alex / Tessa,

Following up with the first set of artifacts — attached are sanitized samples and a short explanation of each column. Notes:

- scim_delta_sample_30d.csv (attached): contains a sequence of SCIM operations (POST/PUT/DELETE), timestamp (UTC), actor_id (internal id), target_user_id (hashed), and attributes changed. We replaced emails with SHA256 hashes and included a mapping table internally (not shared).

Sample rows (sanitized):
operation,timestamp,actor_id,target_user_hash,attributes
POST,2026-11-12T14:05:23Z,svc_provisioner_01,3f2a9c...,displayName;groups
PATCH,2026-11-21T02:17:10Z,ad_sync_job,9b8e1d...,groups
DELETE,2026-11-29T23:58:01Z,console_admin_02,7a4d6b...,

- saml_assertion_snippets.txt (attached): three short snippets: interactive user (Okta), service account (provisioned CI user), and SSO delegated flow for partner integrations. We include attribute names we assert (email, groups, role).

- rbac_owner_matrix_v1.xlsx (attached): role name, role_id, owner (internal email), last_attestation_date, approval_ticket_id. We pulled last attestation events from our governance tooling.

A few caveats:
- We do not share raw user emails or IDs without an NDA/legal approval; salted hashes should be sufficient for SIG review.
- Service accounts are scoped via short-lived tokens and scoped roles; the SAML snippets show audience restrictions.

If you want a short walkthrough, I'm available for a 30-minute call tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com

---
[Attachments: scim_delta_sample_30d.csv (CSV), saml_assertion_snippets.txt (TXT), rbac_owner_matrix_v1.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Alex Bryce <alex.bryce@quantumhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T11:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG request: RBAC custodian mapping + SCIM delta artifacts

Naomi, Tessa — this is great, thanks for the prompt delivery and the sanitized approach. Two quick follow-ups:

1) Can you include the approval workflow artifact for role attestation (a ticket or audit log showing the approver and timestamp)? A screenshot of the attestation UI is fine if a link is not possible.
2) For the service-account SAML snippet, can you confirm the audience URI and whether the assertion contains a 'roles' claim or if groups are used instead? We need this for our control mapping.

If you can drop those two items by tomorrow EOD, we can mark the SIG as complete on our side.

Thanks — Alex

Alex — quick note: attaching a screenshot of the attestation UI and a link to the governance ticket that shows the recent role attestation (see attachments and HubSpot link).

- The attestation UI screenshot shows owner, attestation date, and approver comment.
- Service-account SAML assertions use the audience URI urn:redwood:service and we include 'groups' claims rather than a dedicated 'roles' claim; mapping to roles happens in our authorization layer (we've included a short note in the commentary).

Let us know if you want a 20-min call to walk through the attachments.
